subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu Count the Mangoes
hook: Help Arjun count mangoes in the orchard with his clever parrot friend Mitthu!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old who loves counting

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A cheerful parrot who repeats numbers and helps Arjun count

slides.title: Arjun and Mitthu Visit the Orchard
slides.storyContext: Arjun and his parrot Mitthu arrive at Grandpa's mango orchard on a sunny morning. Mitthu sits on Arjun's shoulder, excited to play. Grandpa says, 'I need help counting mangoes! Can you count them all?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun and Mitthu go to count mangoes with Grandpa.

image.alt: Arjun and Mitthu Visit the Orchard — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: One Mango Falls
slides.storyContext: Arjun walks under the first tree. Plop! One big ripe mango falls into his basket. Mitthu chirps, 'One! One! One!' and flaps his wings happily.

points.label: Number 1
points.text: One mango. Just one. Mitthu repeats: 'One!'

slides.inSimpleWords: One mango falls. That is the number 1.

image.alt: One Mango Falls — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Two Mangoes Together
slides.storyContext: They move to the next tree. Another mango drops. Now Arjun has two mangoes in his basket. Mitthu counts: 'One... two! One... two!'

points.label: Number 2
points.text: Two mangoes now. We count: 1, 2.

example.problem: How many mangoes in the basket now?

slides.inSimpleWords: Two mangoes make the number 2.

image.alt: Two Mangoes Together — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Three, Four, Five Mangoes!
slides.storyContext: Arjun keeps walking. Plop! Plop! Plop! Three more mangoes fall one by one. His basket grows heavier. Mitthu counts excitedly: 'Three! Four! Five! My turn: one, two, three, four, five!'

points.text: Three, four, five — we count higher!

slides.inSimpleWords: Three, four, five mangoes are here now.

image.alt: Three, Four, Five Mangoes! — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Six, Seven Mangoes
slides.storyContext: The tree is so full! One more mango... then another! Arjun counts with his fingers. Mitthu bounces on his head. 'Six! Seven! We're getting so many!'

points.label: Counting with fingers
points.text: Hold up fingers to count: 1, 2, 3... 6, 7

example.solution: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven

slides.inSimpleWords: Six and seven come after five.

image.alt: Six, Seven Mangoes — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Eight and Nine!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu find two more mangoes hidden under leaves. 'Eight!' shouts Mitthu. 'Nine!' says Arjun, holding up the last one. The basket is almost full!

points.label: 8 and 9
points.text: After 7 comes 8, then 9

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight and nine are the last big numbers.

image.alt: Eight and Nine! — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Count With Mitthu
slides.storyContext: Mitthu flies around the basket in circles and chirps a challenge: 'Arjun! Close your eyes and I'll drop mangoes one by one. You count them without looking!'

points.label: Listening count
points.text: Count by hearing sounds, not just seeing

example.problem: Mitthu drops 5 mangoes. Count them by sound.

slides.inSimpleWords: Count things even when you can't see them.

image.alt: Count With Mitthu — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Grandpa Counts All
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu show Grandpa the full basket. Grandpa claps and counts: 'One... two... three... all the way to nine! You counted perfectly!' Mitthu does a happy dance.

points.label: All together
points.text: Numbers 1 to 9 in order

slides.inSimpleWords: The numbers 1 to 9 go in order.

image.alt: Grandpa Counts All — Numbers from 1 to 9

slides.title: Numbers 1 to 9
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sings a little song sitting on the basket: 'One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine! Count them, find them, everywhere!' Arjun claps along.

points.label: We use them
points.text: To count mangoes, fingers, toys, anything!

slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers 1 to 9 help us count everything.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Toy Party
hook: Watch how Arjun and Mitthu bring toys together and discover addition!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old learning to add toys

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A clever parrot who loves combining things

slides.title: Time for a Toy Party!
slides.storyContext: Arjun sits on the floor with a pile of toys. Mitthu lands beside him. 'Let's make a big pile!' says Arjun. 'When we put toys together, we add!' chirps Mitthu wisely.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun and Mitthu put toys together to play.

image.alt: Time for a Toy Party! — Addition

slides.title: Two Toy Cars
slides.storyContext: Arjun places one red toy car on the floor. Then he picks up one blue toy car. 'Look, Mitthu! One car... and one more car!' Mitthu hops up and down. 'That's two cars now!'

points.text: One car plus one car makes two

slides.inSimpleWords: One plus one makes two.

slides.title: Adding on Fingers
slides.storyContext: Arjun holds up one finger on his left hand. 'One car here.' Then one finger on his right hand. 'One car here.' He brings them together. 'One plus one makes two!' Mitthu claps.

points.label: Count on fingers
points.text: Hold up fingers to add

slides.inSimpleWords: Use your fingers to add numbers.

slides.title: Two Balls and One More
slides.storyContext: Arjun rolls out two red balls. 'Two balls,' he counts. Then he rolls one yellow ball next to them. 'And... one more!' Mitthu flies over. 'That's three balls total! Two plus one is three!'

points.text: Two plus one makes three

slides.inSimpleWords: Two plus one makes three.

image.alt: Two Balls and One More — Addition

slides.title: Blocks Stack Taller
slides.storyContext: Arjun stacks three blue blocks. Then he stacks two more blocks on top. 'Three blocks... then two more blocks!' He counts them all. Mitthu looks amazed. 'Five blocks now! Three plus two is five!'

points.text: Three plus two makes five

slides.inSimpleWords: Three plus two makes five.

slides.title: The Teddy and Dolls
slides.storyContext: Arjun lines up one teddy bear. Next to it, he arranges three dolls. 'One teddy... three dolls... let's add!' One teddy plus three dolls makes four friends! Mitthu nods. 'One plus three is four!'

points.text: One plus three makes four

slides.inSimpleWords: One plus three makes four.

slides.title: Make Your Own Addition
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges Arjun: 'Pick any two groups of toys and add them together! Count what you get!' Arjun picks two toy trains and three toy elephants. 'Two plus three... that's five!'

points.label: Try adding
points.text: Pick toys and add them to find the answer

slides.inSimpleWords: You can add any two groups together.

slides.title: Toy Party Gets Bigger!
slides.storyContext: Mitthu suggests, 'Let's add bigger numbers now!' Arjun arranges four building blocks and four toy cars. 'Four plus four...' He counts the whole pile slowly. '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8! That's eight!'

points.text: Four plus four makes eight

slides.inSimpleWords: Four plus four makes eight.

slides.title: We Can Add!
slides.storyContext: All the toys are in one big happy pile. Mitthu sings: 'When we put toys together, we add! One plus one, two plus one, three plus two... addition is putting things with things!' Arjun giggles.

points.label: Addition means
points.text: Putting two groups together

slides.inSimpleWords: Addition is putting groups together to count.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Treat Sharing
hook: Discover subtraction when Arjun and Mitthu share treats!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old learning to take away and share

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A thoughtful parrot helping with sharing

slides.title: Treats in the Bowl
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom gives him a bowl with five yummy biscuits. Mitthu smells them and says, 'Wow! We need to share these!' Arjun nods happily. 'Let's take some away and count what's left!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun has treats to share with Mitthu.

slides.title: One Biscuit Away
slides.storyContext: Arjun counts five biscuits in the bowl. 'Five!' Then he takes one biscuit out for Mitthu. 'I'm taking one away.' He counts what's left: 'One, two, three, four. That's four biscuits now!'

points.text: When we take one away from five, four is left

slides.inSimpleWords: Five minus one leaves four.

slides.title: Counting Down
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'When we take away, we count backwards!' Arjun had four biscuits. He gives one to his little sister. 'Four, three... three left!' Mitthu nods wisely. 'We count down from four to three!'

points.label: Take away means
points.text: Remove and count what stays

slides.inSimpleWords: When we take away, we count backwards.

slides.title: Three Biscuits, One Crumb
slides.storyContext: Arjun has three biscuits on his plate. 'Crunch! Crunch!' He eats one. Mitthu watches and counts: 'You had three. You ate one. Now you have... one, two. That's two left!'

points.text: Three take away one is two

slides.inSimpleWords: Three minus one leaves two.

slides.title: Taking Away More
slides.storyContext: Arjun shows Mitthu six fruits: four apples and two oranges. 'Let's take away two apples!' He moves them aside. Mitthu counts: 'One, two, three, four fruits stay. Six take away two is four!'

points.text: Six take away two is four

slides.inSimpleWords: Six minus two leaves four.

slides.title: Share with Friends
slides.storyContext: Arjun has five toy cars. His friend Ravi comes to play. 'Let's give Ravi two cars!' says Arjun. He counts what he has left: 'One, two, three. Three cars still mine. Five take away two is three!'

points.text: Five take away two is three

slides.inSimpleWords: Five minus two leaves three.

slides.title: Mitthu's Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sets up a challenge: 'I have seven seeds. I eat three. How many are left?' Arjun counts carefully on his fingers. '7... take away 3... is 4!' Mitthu chirps happily.

points.label: Try it yourself
points.text: Use fingers or count backwards

slides.inSimpleWords: Seven minus three leaves four.

slides.title: Empty Bowl
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom makes more treats! Now there are eight samosas in a plate. Arjun and Mitthu eat them all one by one. 'Eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one...' Finally: 'Zero! All gone!'

points.label: Subtracting all
points.text: If we take away everything, nothing is left

slides.inSimpleWords: Taking away everything leaves zero.

slides.title: Taking Away
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on Arjun's shoulder. 'Subtraction means taking away! Five take away two is three. Three take away one is two. We count down and find what's left!'

points.label: Subtraction is
points.text: Taking away and counting what stays

slides.inSimpleWords: Subtraction is taking away to find what's left.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu Find Shapes Everywhere
hook: Search the neighborhood with Arjun and Mitthu to find circles, squares, and triangles!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old discovering shapes

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A shape-loving parrot who points out patterns

slides.title: A Shape Hunt Begins!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu look out the window. Mitthu cries out, 'Arjun! Look! Shapes everywhere!' Arjun's eyes grow wide. 'Let's find them all!' Off they go on a shape adventure through their neighborhood.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun and Mitthu go hunting for shapes.

image.alt: A Shape Hunt Begins! — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Circle, Circle!
slides.storyContext: They walk to the park. Mitthu points at the big round clock on the tower. 'That's a circle, Arjun! Round all the way around!' Then they spot a ball rolling by. 'Another circle!' Arjun laughs.

points.label: Circle
points.text: Round like a ball or a plate

slides.inSimpleWords: Circles are round like a ball.

slides.title: Square Windows
slides.storyContext: At the shopkeeper's house, Arjun points up. 'Look! Four sides, all the same!' Mitthu agrees, 'That's a square, Arjun. See? The window is a square. Four corners, four sides that are all the same size!'

points.label: Square
points.text: Four equal sides, four corners

example.solution: A square has four equal sides

slides.inSimpleWords: Squares have four equal sides.

slides.title: Triangle Pizza!
slides.storyContext: Arjun's stomach rumbles. They peek into the pizza shop. 'Look, Mitthu! Triangles!' The pizza slices are triangles with three sides and three corners. Mitthu hops: 'Three! That's why it's called a triangle!'

points.label: Triangle
points.text: Three sides and three corners

slides.inSimpleWords: Triangles have three sides and three corners.

slides.title: Rectangle Doors
slides.storyContext: They pass a shop with a tall door. 'That's not a square!' says Arjun. Mitthu nods wisely. 'It's a rectangle! It has four sides, but two are longer. Long and short sides, four corners!'

points.label: Rectangle
points.text: Four sides, but two long and two short

example.problem: Is this door a square or rectangle?
example.solution: Rectangle — it's taller than it is wide

slides.inSimpleWords: Rectangles are longer on two sides.

slides.title: Star in the Sky
slides.storyContext: It's getting evening. Mitthu points up at a drawn star on a poster. 'A star! It has pointy corners!' Arjun counts: 'One, two, three, four, five... five pointy corners! That's a star!'

points.label: Star
points.text: Five pointy corners

slides.inSimpleWords: Stars have five pointy corners.

image.alt: Star in the Sky — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Mitthu's Shape Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu creates a challenge: 'I'll describe a shape. You guess it! Round and flat, no corners at all.' Arjun jumps up. 'A circle!' Mitthu continues: 'Four equal sides and four corners!' Arjun shouts, 'A square!'

points.label: Guess the shape
points.text: Listen to clues about sides and corners

slides.inSimpleWords: You can guess shapes by counting sides.

image.alt: Mitthu's Shape Game — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Shapes All Around
slides.storyContext: Arjun looks around and spots more shapes: 'The biscuit tin is a square! The car wheel is a circle! The tent is a triangle!' Mitthu claps his wings. 'Shapes are everywhere, Arjun! Everywhere!'

points.label: All around us
points.text: Circles, squares, triangles, rectangles, stars

slides.inSimpleWords: We see shapes in everything around us.

image.alt: Shapes All Around — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: All the Shapes
slides.storyContext: Back home, Mitthu summarizes on Arjun's shoulder: 'Circle is round. Square has four equal sides. Rectangle has four sides but two are longer. Triangle has three sides. Star has five points! Remember them?'

points.label: Five main shapes
points.text: Circle, Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Star

points.label: Count the sides
points.text: 3 = triangle, 4 = square/rectangle, 0 = circle, 5 = star

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes are circles, squares, rectangles, triangles, and stars.

image.alt: All the Shapes — Shapes Around Us

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu at the Market
hook: Help Arjun and Mitthu buy yummy treats using rupees!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old buying treats at the market

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A clever parrot who counts rupees

slides.title: Market Day!
slides.storyContext: Arjun's grandpa gives him 10 rupees! 'Let's go to the market, Mitthu!' Off they go, jingling coins in a little pouch. The market is full of colors and smells. Mitthu perches on Arjun's shoulder, excited.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun has money to buy things at the market.

slides.title: One Rupee Coin
slides.storyContext: Arjun looks at his coins. Mitthu points with his wing. 'That shiny one! See the number 1? That's one rupee!' Arjun holds it up. It's small and round. 'One rupee, Mitthu!'

points.label: ₹1 coin
points.text: The smallest coin has the number 1

slides.inSimpleWords: One rupee is a small shiny coin.

slides.title: Five Rupees!
slides.storyContext: Arjun picks up a bigger coin. 'This one feels heavier!' Mitthu reads: 'That says 5! Five rupees. It's worth more than one rupee because the number is bigger!'

points.label: ₹5 coin
points.text: Worth more than one rupee

example.problem: Which is worth more: 1 rupee or 5 rupees?

slides.inSimpleWords: Five rupees are worth more than one rupee.

slides.title: At the Fruit Stall
slides.storyContext: They stop at the apple stall. 'How much for an apple?' asks Arjun. 'Two rupees!' says the seller. Arjun hands over two coins: one rupee and one rupee. 'That's two rupees total!' Mitthu nods approvingly.

points.label: Buying costs money
points.text: Apple costs 2 rupees

slides.inSimpleWords: You give money to buy things.

slides.title: Counting Rupees
slides.storyContext: At the snack shop, samosas cost 3 rupees each. Arjun has 10 rupees. 'Mitthu, I can buy 3 samosas! One samosa is 3 rupees, so I need 3 rupees three times!' He counts carefully: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 rupees used.

points.label: Count rupees
points.text: One samosa = 3 rupees, two = 6 rupees, three = 9 rupees

example.problem: Samosa costs 3 rupees. How many can you buy with 10 rupees?
example.solution: Three samosas costs 9 rupees. 1 rupee is left.

slides.inSimpleWords: Count rupees to know what you can buy.

slides.title: The Sweet Shop
slides.storyContext: Next, they visit the sweet shop. 'Mitthu, look! Gulab jamuns!' Arjun points. 'How much?' he asks. 'Four rupees for one!' says the shopkeeper. Arjun gives four coins carefully. 'That's 4 rupees for one gulab jamun!'

points.label: 4 rupees
points.text: Enough to buy one treat

slides.inSimpleWords: Four rupees can buy one sweet.

slides.title: How Much Money Left?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'You started with 10 rupees. You spent 3 on samosa, 4 on gulab jamun. How much is left?' Arjun counts on his fingers. '3 + 4 is 7. 10 - 7 is 3. Three rupees left!'

points.label: Count what's left
points.text: Subtract what you spent from what you had

example.problem: Started with 10 rupees. Spent 7. How much is left?

slides.inSimpleWords: Count what money is left after spending.

slides.title: One Last Purchase
slides.storyContext: Arjun sees candy. 'Mitthu, just 3 rupees left. Candy costs 2 rupees!' He buys one piece of candy. 'Now I have 1 rupee left!' Mitthu smiles. 'You spent your rupees wisely, Arjun!'

points.label: Spend wisely
points.text: Count your rupees before you buy

slides.inSimpleWords: Count your money before you buy.

slides.title: Rupees and Shopping
slides.storyContext: Walking home, Mitthu recaps: 'One rupee, five rupees, coins and notes — we use them to buy things we want! Count your rupees, know what things cost, and spend wisely!' Arjun munches his apple happily.

points.label: Money is for buying
points.text: We earn or get rupees to buy things

points.label: Count before spending
points.text: Know how many rupees you have and what things cost

slides.inSimpleWords: Rupees are money we use to buy things.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Day
hook: Follow Arjun and Mitthu through a whole day and learn about time!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old learning to tell time through his day

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A bird who notices time and time of day

slides.title: Morning Alarm!
slides.storyContext: Ring! Ring! Arjun's alarm goes off. Mitthu yawns on the window sill. 'Good morning! The sun is rising. It's early morning!' says Mitthu. Arjun stretches and rubs his eyes. A new day is beginning!
slides.inSimpleWords: Mornings start when the sun rises.

slides.title: Breakfast Time
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom serves breakfast. 'It's 8 o'clock!' she says, pointing to the kitchen clock. Mitthu perches on the table. 'See the short hand and long hand? The short one is on 8, the long one is on 12. That's eight o'clock in the morning!'

points.label: 8 o'clock
points.text: Time for breakfast in the morning

slides.inSimpleWords: 8 o'clock is breakfast time.

slides.title: School Time
slides.storyContext: Arjun gets ready. 'It's 9 o'clock! Time for school!' He picks up his bag. Mitthu shows him the clock: 'The short hand moved to 9, the long hand is still at 12. That means 9 o'clock!'

points.label: 9 o'clock
points.text: Time for school in the morning

example.problem: Where is the short hand at 9 o'clock?
example.solution: At the 9. The long hand is at the 12.

slides.inSimpleWords: The short hand shows the hour.

slides.title: Sunny Afternoon
slides.storyContext: At noon, the sun is right above. 'It's 12 o'clock! Noon!' says the teacher. Mitthu nods. 'The short hand and long hand are both on 12. That means 12 o'clock — the middle of the day! Very bright, very hot!'

points.label: 12 o'clock (noon)
points.text: Middle of the day, the sun is highest

slides.inSimpleWords: 12 o'clock is the middle of the day.

slides.title: Lunch at One
slides.storyContext: At lunch time, it's 1 o'clock. Arjun eats with Mitthu. 'Look at the clock, Mitthu! The short hand is on 1, the long hand is on 12. One o'clock — lunchtime!'

points.label: 1 o'clock
points.text: Afternoon lunchtime

example.solution: 1 o'clock. Short hand on 1, long hand on 12.

slides.inSimpleWords: 1 o'clock is lunch and early afternoon.

slides.title: Evening Play
slides.storyContext: It's 4 o'clock in the afternoon. 'Time to play outside!' says Arjun. The sun is getting lower. Mitthu watches the clock: 'The short hand is on 4, long hand on 12. Four o'clock — playtime in the evening!'

points.label: 4 o'clock
points.text: Afternoon playtime

slides.inSimpleWords: 4 o'clock is afternoon playtime.

slides.title: Sunset and Dinner
slides.storyContext: Mitthu flies home as the sun sets. 'Look! It's 6 o'clock! Dinner time!' The short hand is on 6. It's getting dark. Mitthu says, 'The day is ending. Soon night will come!'

points.label: 6 o'clock
points.text: Evening dinner time

slides.inSimpleWords: 6 o'clock is dinner and evening time.

slides.title: Bedtime
slides.storyContext: At 8 o'clock, Arjun yawns. 'Time for bed!' His mom tucks him in. Mitthu sits on the headboard. 'Look, Arjun. The short hand is on 8 again. 8 o'clock at night. Time to sleep and dream!'

points.label: 8 o'clock
points.text: Night bedtime

slides.inSimpleWords: 8 o'clock at night is bedtime.

slides.title: A Whole Day
slides.storyContext: Mitthu whispers as Arjun drifts to sleep: 'Morning, breakfast, school, noon, lunch, playtime, dinner, sleep — a whole day! The clock's short hand moves from hour to hour. That's how we know what time it is!'

points.label: The short hand
points.text: Shows the hour (1, 2, 3... 12)

points.label: The long hand
points.text: Shows the minutes (on 12 at each hour)

points.label: A whole day
points.text: Starts at morning, ends at night

slides.inSimpleWords: Time tells us when things happen during the day.

subject: The World Around Us
title: Arjun and Mitthu Discover Body Parts
hook: Learn about your amazing body parts with Arjun and Mitthu!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old discovering his own body

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A parrot with wings who helps Arjun learn about bodies

slides.title: Bodies Are Amazing!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu stand in front of the mirror. 'Look at us!' says Arjun. Mitthu spreads his wings. 'We both have bodies, Arjun! But they're different. Let's explore yours together!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Our bodies have many special parts.

slides.title: Head and Brain
slides.storyContext: Arjun touches his head. 'This is my head!' He points to his forehead, cheeks, and chin. 'And inside here is my brain. It helps me think and remember!' Mitthu taps his own head with his beak. 'My head helps me think too!'

points.label: Head
points.text: Top of your body, has face and brain inside

slides.inSimpleWords: Your head has your brain inside.

slides.title: Eyes See
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to his eyes. 'With these, I see colors! I see you, Mitthu!' He blinks. 'I have two eyes.' Mitthu nods wisely. 'Eyes help us see everything around us — trees, sky, food, friends!'

points.label: Eyes
points.text: Two eyes help us see the world

slides.inSimpleWords: Eyes help you see everything.

slides.title: Nose, Mouth, Ears
slides.storyContext: Arjun traces his nose. 'My nose helps me smell yummy food!' He opens his mouth. 'My mouth helps me eat and talk!' Then he points to his ears. 'And my ears help me hear you, Mitthu!' Mitthu chirps happily.

points.label: Nose, mouth, ears
points.text: Smell, eat/talk, hear

slides.inSimpleWords: Nose smells, mouth eats and talks, ears hear.

slides.title: Heart and Lungs
slides.storyContext: Arjun puts his hand on his chest. 'Feel that, Mitthu?' Thump-thump, thump-thump. 'That's my heart beating! It pumps blood to every part of my body. And here I breathe with my lungs — in and out, in and out!'

points.label: Heart and lungs
points.text: Inside your chest — heart beats, lungs breathe

example.solution: It beats and sends blood everywhere

slides.inSimpleWords: Your heart beats and pumps blood.

slides.title: Arms and Hands
slides.storyContext: Arjun stretches his arms up high. 'My arms help me reach!' He moves them around. 'And my hands — I have fingers! Five on each hand!' He wiggles them. Mitthu watches as Arjun claps. 'We hug with arms and pick things up with hands!'

points.label: Arms and hands
points.text: Two arms, two hands with five fingers each

slides.inSimpleWords: Arms and hands help you pick things up.

slides.title: Legs and Feet
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps and runs. 'My legs help me jump and walk! And my feet have five toes each — just like my fingers!' He wiggles his toes. 'Without legs, I couldn't run to play!' Mitthu flaps his wings in agreement.

points.label: Legs and feet
points.text: Two legs, two feet with five toes each

slides.inSimpleWords: Legs and feet help you walk and run.

slides.title: Bones and Skin
slides.storyContext: Arjun touches his arm and feels the bone inside. 'I have bones inside that hold me up!' He looks at his skin. 'And this skin covers everything and protects me. Mitthu, do you have bones too?' 'Yes! All animals have bodies with special parts!'

points.label: Bones and skin
points.text: Bones inside hold us up, skin covers and protects

slides.inSimpleWords: Bones hold you up, skin protects you.

slides.title: Your Body Is Wonderful!
slides.storyContext: Arjun hugs himself. 'My body is amazing! Head to toes, inside and out!' Mitthu perches on his shoulder. 'Head, face, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, heart, lungs, arms, hands, legs, feet, bones, skin — every part does something important for you!'

points.label: Body parts and jobs
points.text: Eyes see, nose smells, mouth eats, ears hear, heart beats, lungs breathe, legs run

points.label: Take care of it
points.text: Eat well, sleep, play, exercise, stay clean

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body has many amazing parts that work together.

image.alt: Your Body Is Wonderful! — My Body

subject: The World Around Us
title: Arjun and Mitthu Meet Animal Friends
hook: Explore the wonderful animals living all around us!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old meeting different animals

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A helpful parrot who introduces his animal friends

slides.title: A Trip to the Zoo!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu walk to the zoo. 'There are so many animals here!' Mitthu nods excitedly. 'I have friends everywhere — in the sky, on the ground, in the water! Let's meet them all!'
slides.inSimpleWords: There are many animals around us.

image.alt: A Trip to the Zoo! — Animals Around Us

slides.title: The Lion Roars!
slides.storyContext: ROARRR! A big lion with a golden mane sits proudly. 'That's Leo, the king of animals!' says Mitthu. Arjun steps back carefully. 'He's big and strong! His roar is so loud!' The lion's sharp teeth shine in the sun.

points.label: Lion
points.text: A big, strong animal with a mane who roars

slides.inSimpleWords: Lions are big, strong animals that roar.

image.alt: The Lion Roars! — Animals Around Us

slides.title: Elephant's Long Trunk
slides.storyContext: Near the water is a giant elephant! 'Look at that long trunk!' Arjun gasps. The elephant uses it to grab peanuts and spray water. 'An elephant is the biggest land animal, Arjun. Its trunk has many uses!' explains Mitthu.

points.label: Elephant
points.text: Huge animal with a long trunk and big ears

example.problem: What does an elephant use its trunk for?
example.solution: To grab food, spray water, and hold things

slides.inSimpleWords: Elephants have long trunks and are very big.

image.alt: Elephant's Long Trunk — Animals Around Us

slides.title: Monkey Swings
slides.storyContext: Suddenly, a monkey swings from a tree branch! 'Ooh ooh ooh!' it chatters. Arjun laughs. 'So playful!' The monkey has four hands and a long tail. 'Monkeys are clever and love to jump and swing!' says Mitthu.

points.label: Monkey
points.text: Clever animal that swings and plays

slides.inSimpleWords: Monkeys swing and play in trees.

slides.title: Tiger and Stripes
slides.storyContext: A magnificent orange tiger with black stripes walks past. 'Beautiful!' whispers Arjun. 'Those stripes help it hide in tall grass,' explains Mitthu. 'Tigers are wild cats — strong hunters with sharp claws and teeth!'

points.label: Tiger
points.text: Striped wild cat, powerful and beautiful

example.problem: Why does a tiger have stripes?
example.solution: To hide in grass while hunting

slides.inSimpleWords: Tigers are striped and very strong.

image.alt: Tiger and Stripes — Animals Around Us

slides.title: Parrot Family
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sees other parrots in a tree. 'Look, Arjun! My cousins!' Colorful parrots — red, blue, green — sit together. 'Parrots are smart! We can talk and repeat words. We love shiny things and fruit!' Mitthu preens his feathers proudly.

points.label: Parrot
points.text: Colorful bird that talks and is very smart

slides.inSimpleWords: Parrots are colorful and can talk.

slides.title: Crocodile in Water
slides.storyContext: In the pond, Arjun spots a crocodile with bumpy skin floating still. 'That one is dangerous!' warns Mitthu. 'Crocodiles are reptiles that live in water. They have sharp teeth and move quietly — you won't hear them coming!'

points.label: Crocodile
points.text: Lives in water, bumpy skin, very quiet and dangerous

slides.inSimpleWords: Crocodiles live in water and are dangerous.

image.alt: Crocodile in Water — Animals Around Us

slides.title: Cow and Buffalo
slides.storyContext: In the farm area, a gentle cow moos. 'Mooooo!' And a big buffalo stands nearby. 'These animals give us milk!' says Mitthu kindly. 'Cows and buffalo are helpful. Farmers take care of them, and they give us food!'

points.label: Cow and Buffalo
points.text: Gentle farm animals that give us milk

slides.inSimpleWords: Cows and buffalo give us milk.

image.alt: Cow and Buffalo — Animals Around Us

slides.title: Animals All Around
slides.storyContext: As the sun sets, Arjun and Mitthu leave the zoo. 'We saw lions, elephants, monkeys, tigers, parrots, crocodiles, cows, and more!' Mitthu smiles. 'Animals live everywhere — in jungles, forests, water, farms, and in our homes! They're all important!'

points.label: Different animals
points.text: Big, small, wild, tame, fly, swim, run

points.label: Their homes
points.text: Jungles, forests, water, farms, sky, trees, homes

slides.inSimpleWords: Many different animals live all around us.

image.alt: Animals All Around — Animals Around Us

subject: The World Around Us
title: Arjun and Mitthu Explore Plants
hook: Discover the amazing green plants that grow everywhere!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old learning about plants

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A nature-loving parrot who knows all about plants

slides.title: Welcome to the Garden!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu walk into Grandma's garden. Everything is green and colorful! 'Look, Mitthu! Plants everywhere!' Mitthu nods happily. 'Plants are living things that grow in soil and need sun and water. Let me show you!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Plants are living things that grow.

image.alt: Welcome to the Garden! — Plants Around Us

slides.title: Parts of a Plant
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points with his wing. 'Every plant has roots, a stem, leaves, and sometimes flowers or fruit.' Arjun bends to look. 'The roots are in the ground!' Mitthu nods. 'They sip water from the soil to feed the plant!'

points.label: Plant parts
points.text: Roots (underground), stem, leaves, flowers, fruit

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants have roots, stems, and leaves.

image.alt: Parts of a Plant — Plants Around Us

slides.title: Leaves Are Green
slides.storyContext: Arjun touches a soft green leaf. 'So smooth! So green!' Mitthu explains, 'Leaves are green because they have something called chlorophyll. They catch sunlight and help the plant make food! Green leaves mean a healthy plant!'

points.label: Leaves
points.text: Green, catch sunlight, make food for the plant

example.solution: They have chlorophyll to catch sunlight

slides.inSimpleWords: Green leaves catch sunlight for the plant.

image.alt: Leaves Are Green — Plants Around Us

slides.title: Flowers Bloom
slides.storyContext: Arjun's eyes widen at the sight of flowers — red roses, yellow sunflowers, pink tulips! 'So pretty!' he gasps. Mitthu lands on a sunflower. 'Flowers are where plants make seeds. Bees and birds like me drink nectar from them!'

points.label: Flowers
points.text: Colorful, have seeds, attract bees and birds

slides.inSimpleWords: Flowers are colorful and smell sweet.

slides.title: Fruits and Seeds
slides.storyContext: In the orchard, mango trees hang heavy with fruit. 'Look, Arjun! Mangoes!' Mitthu points. 'After flowers, fruits grow with seeds inside. The seeds can grow into new plants! That's how apple trees, mango trees, and banana plants spread!'

points.label: Fruits and seeds
points.text: Fruits protect seeds that can grow into new plants

example.solution: A seed that can grow into a new mango tree

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits have seeds that grow into new plants.

image.alt: Fruits and Seeds — Plants Around Us

slides.title: Big Trees
slides.storyContext: They walk to an old banyan tree with a huge trunk and drooping branches. 'Wow! This tree is so old and big!' Arjun marvels. Mitthu lands on a thick branch. 'This tree is home to many animals like me! Big trees give shade and clean air for everyone!'

points.label: Trees
points.text: Biggest plants, give shade, clean air, homes for animals

slides.inSimpleWords: Trees are big plants that give us shade.

slides.title: Watering Plants
slides.storyContext: Arjun helps Grandma water the plants with a watering can. 'Plants need water from rain and from us!' she says. Arjun pours gently. Mitthu watches. 'Roots drink the water. Water travels up the stem to leaves and flowers. That's how plants grow!'

points.label: Watering plants
points.text: Plants need water to grow healthy

example.problem: What does a plant need to grow?

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants need water and sunlight to grow.

slides.title: Vegetables We Eat
slides.storyContext: Grandma shows Arjun the vegetable patch. 'Carrots, tomatoes, spinach, cucumber — all from plants!' Arjun picks a ripe tomato. Mitthu chirps, 'Plants give us food to eat! Vegetables, fruits, grains — everything comes from plants!'

points.label: Food from plants
points.text: Vegetables, fruits, grains, nuts, all from plants

slides.inSimpleWords: We eat vegetables and fruits from plants.

image.alt: Vegetables We Eat — Plants Around Us

slides.title: Plants Everywhere
slides.storyContext: As they walk home, Mitthu summarizes: 'Plants have roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits. They need sun, water, and soil. They give us food, oxygen, shade, and beauty! Plants are amazing and so important!'

points.label: What plants do
points.text: Give food, oxygen, shade; make Earth beautiful

points.label: How to help
points.text: Water them, give them sunlight, pull weeds

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants are amazing and we need them to live.

subject: The World Around Us
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Food Adventure
hook: Discover where yummy food comes from with Arjun and Mitthu!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old learning about healthy food

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A parrot who knows all about different foods

slides.title: What's for Dinner?
slides.storyContext: Arjun's tummy rumbles. 'I'm hungry, Mitthu!' Mitthu flies around the kitchen. 'Let's explore food together! We'll learn where different foods come from and what makes our bodies strong!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Food gives our bodies energy and strength.

image.alt: What's for Dinner? — Food We Eat

slides.title: Grains Keep Us Going
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom makes rice and roti. 'Grains give us energy!' she says. Arjun tastes fluffy rice. Mitthu nods. 'Rice, wheat, maize — grains come from plants. They make our bodies strong and give us power to run and play!'

points.label: Grains
points.text: Rice, wheat, roti, bread — give us energy

slides.inSimpleWords: Grains like rice and roti give us energy.

image.alt: Grains Keep Us Going — Food We Eat

slides.title: Fruits and Vegetables
slides.storyContext: At the market, colorful fruits and vegetables shine! Bright red tomatoes, yellow bananas, green spinach, orange carrots. 'These make us healthy!' says Mitthu. Arjun picks a ripe apple. 'Fruits and vegetables have vitamins and minerals our bodies need!'

points.label: Fruits and vegetables
points.text: Apples, bananas, carrots, tomatoes — keep us healthy

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits and vegetables keep you healthy.

image.alt: Fruits and Vegetables — Food We Eat

slides.title: Protein Power
slides.storyContext: At lunch, Arjun eats dal and paneer. Mitthu pecks at some seeds. 'These foods have protein!' says Mitthu wisely. 'Protein helps our muscles grow strong. Dal, paneer, eggs, nuts, beans — all have protein to make us healthy and strong!'

points.label: Protein foods
points.text: Dal, paneer, eggs, nuts, fish, chicken — build strong muscles

slides.inSimpleWords: Proteins help your muscles grow strong.

slides.title: Milk and Dairy
slides.storyContext: Arjun drinks a glass of cold milk. 'Yum!' Mitthu explains, 'Milk comes from cows and buffalo. Milk, yogurt, cheese — these make bones and teeth strong! Calcium from dairy keeps you healthy!'

points.label: Dairy products
points.text: Milk, yogurt, cheese — strong bones and teeth

example.solution: Milk and dairy products with calcium

slides.inSimpleWords: Milk makes your bones and teeth strong.

image.alt: Milk and Dairy — Food We Eat

slides.title: Sweet Treats in Moderation
slides.storyContext: Grandma makes jaggery and dates. 'A little sweet is okay!' she says. Arjun licks a drop. Mitthu adds, 'Too much sugar isn't good for teeth. But some sweets, like jaggery and fruit, can be part of a healthy diet!'

points.label: Sweets
points.text: Some sweet (jaggery, dates) is okay, but not too much

slides.inSimpleWords: A little sweet is okay, but not lots.

image.alt: Sweet Treats in Moderation — Food We Eat

slides.title: A Balanced Meal
slides.storyContext: Arjun helps his mom make dinner. 'A healthy meal has everything!' she says. Rice (grain), dal (protein), spinach (vegetable), and milk (dairy). 'That's balanced! Grain, protein, vegetable, and dairy — all together make a perfect meal!'

points.label: Balanced diet
points.text: Grain + protein + fruit/vegetable + dairy = healthy

example.solution: Rice, dal, spinach, and milk all together

slides.inSimpleWords: A balanced meal has different kinds of food.

image.alt: A Balanced Meal — Food We Eat

slides.title: Healthy Snacks
slides.storyContext: After playing, Arjun is hungry. 'Let's snack!' says Mitthu. Grandma offers apple slices, peanuts, and yogurt. 'These are healthy snacks — not junk food! Real food that keeps you strong while you play!'

points.label: Healthy snacks
points.text: Fruits, nuts, yogurt, whole grains — better than junk

slides.inSimpleWords: Snack on fruits, nuts, and yogurt, not junk food.

slides.title: Food and Health
slides.storyContext: At dinner, Mitthu recaps: 'Grains give energy. Fruits and vegetables keep you healthy. Proteins make muscles strong. Milk makes bones strong. A balanced diet from all groups keeps you growing, learning, and happy!'

points.label: Food groups
points.text: Grains, proteins, fruits, vegetables, dairy

points.label: Eat variety
points.text: Different foods for different strengths

slides.inSimpleWords: Different foods help your body grow and stay healthy.

image.alt: Food and Health — Food We Eat

subject: English
title: Arjun and Mitthu Learn Names
hook: Discover naming words — the names of all the things around us!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old learning to name things

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A parrot who loves knowing names of everything

slides.title: What's Your Name?
slides.storyContext: Arjun sits on the grass with his friend Mitthu. 'I'm Arjun. That's my name!' he says proudly. Mitthu chirps, 'And I'm Mitthu! Names are special words we use to call things and people. They're called naming words, or nouns!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words are the names of things.

slides.title: Names of People
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom comes outside. 'I'm Priya!' she waves. Grandma joins them. 'I'm Sudha!' she smiles. Mitthu sings, 'Arjun, Priya, Sudha — all naming words! People have names. Boy, girl, man, woman — these are also naming words that tell us what kind of person!'

points.label: People names
points.text: Arjun, Priya, Sudha, boy, girl, man, woman

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of people are naming words.

slides.title: Names of Animals
slides.storyContext: A dog runs past, wagging its tail. 'That's a dog!' says Arjun. Mitthu nods. 'Dog, cat, parrot, elephant, lion — animal names! And look — a cow in that field! Cow, buffalo, horse, sheep — all naming words for animals!'

points.label: Animal names
points.text: Dog, cat, parrot, lion, cow, buffalo, horse, bird

example.problem: What's the naming word for this?
example.solution: Dog! Or cat, bird, lion — names of animals

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of animals are naming words.

slides.title: Names of Places
slides.storyContext: Arjun points around him. 'Mitthu, we're in the park!' Mitthu agrees, 'Park! And I see school over there. And a hospital. Park, school, hospital, home, market — these are naming words for places where we go!'

points.label: Place names
points.text: Park, school, home, market, hospital, library, city, village

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of places are naming words.

slides.title: Names of Things
slides.storyContext: Arjun picks up a ball. 'Ball!' he says. Mitthu looks around. 'Yes! And tree, flower, bench, water, sun, moon, cloud — all naming words for things we can see or touch!'

points.label: Thing names
points.text: Ball, tree, flower, book, pen, table, house, car

example.solution: Ball, tree, flower, bench, cloud (all naming words)

slides.inSimpleWords: Names of things we can see are naming words.

slides.title: Names of Actions... and No!
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps up. 'Wait, Mitthu! Is jump a naming word?' Mitthu shakes his head. 'No! Jump, run, play, eat — those are action words, not naming words. Naming words are for things, people, places, and animals. Action words are for what we do!'

points.label: Remember
points.text: Naming words = names; Not action words = what we do

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words name things, not actions.

image.alt: Names of Actions... and No! — Naming Words

slides.title: Find the Naming Word
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks a game: 'I say words. You tell me if it's a naming word! Cat... dog... run... tree... happy... book... jump!' Arjun shouts: 'Cat, dog, tree, book are naming words! Run, jump, happy are not!'

points.label: Test yourself
points.text: Cat ✓, run ✗, dog ✓, play ✗, school ✓

example.problem: Is the word happy a naming word?
example.solution: No! It's a describing word, not a name

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words name things — people, places, animals, objects.

image.alt: Find the Naming Word — Naming Words

slides.title: Little Words, Big Naming
slides.storyContext: Grandma brings a small notebook. 'Notebook, pencil, paper — names of things!' She writes Arjun's name. 'Even very small things have names. Ant, grain, seed, drop — even the tiny ones have naming words!'

points.label: Even small things
points.text: Ant, seed, drop, grain — all have naming words

slides.inSimpleWords: Everything has a naming word, big or small.

image.alt: Little Words, Big Naming — Naming Words

slides.title: All About Naming Words
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on the bench with Arjun. 'Naming words are words that name people, animals, places, and things. Arjun, Mitthu, dog, park, tree, ball — all naming words! They tell us what something is called!'

points.label: Naming words (nouns)
points.text: Name people, animals, places, things

points.label: Examples
points.text: Boy, girl, dog, cat, park, home, tree, ball, book

slides.inSimpleWords: Naming words are the names of all things around us.

image.alt: All About Naming Words — Naming Words

subject: English
title: Arjun and Mitthu Play Games with Actions
hook: Learn action words — all the things we do!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old who loves doing actions

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A playful parrot who shows all kinds of actions

slides.title: Let's Play and Do Things!
slides.storyContext: Arjun wakes up ready to play. Mitthu flies into the room. 'Arjun! Let's do things today! Walk, run, jump, play — these are all action words! They tell us what we DO!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Action words are words for things we do.

image.alt: Let's Play and Do Things! — Action Words

slides.title: Moving Actions
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps out of bed. 'I jump!' He walks to the window. 'I walk!' He starts to run. 'I run!' Mitthu flies around his head. 'Jump, walk, run — moving actions! We use these verbs to show movement! Go, skip, hop, climb, roll — all moving actions!'

points.label: Moving actions
points.text: Jump, walk, run, skip, hop, climb, roll, swim

slides.inSimpleWords: Jump, walk, run, skip are moving actions.

slides.title: Eating and Drinking
slides.storyContext: At breakfast, Arjun sits down. 'I eat!' He puts toast in his mouth. Mitthu lands on his plate and pecks. 'I eat too!' Then Arjun drinks milk. 'I drink!' Mitthu sips water. 'Eat, drink, chew, taste — eating actions!'

points.label: Eating actions
points.text: Eat, drink, chew, taste, bite, swallow

example.problem: What action word means to take food into your mouth?
example.solution: Eat! Also: chew, bite, taste, swallow

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat and drink are eating actions.

slides.title: Sound Actions
slides.storyContext: After breakfast, Arjun sings happily. 'I sing!' His friend Ravi shouts from outside. 'Someone talks or shouts!' Mitthu chirps. 'Sing, talk, shout, laugh, cry — sound actions! We make these sounds with our voice!'

points.label: Sound actions
points.text: Sing, talk, shout, laugh, cry, whisper, call

slides.inSimpleWords: Sing, talk, shout are sound actions.

slides.title: Daily Actions
slides.storyContext: At school, Arjun writes his name carefully. 'I write!' His teacher reads from a book. 'Teacher reads!' On the playground, children play. 'We play!' Mitthu watches. 'Write, read, play, draw, color, count — all daily actions at school!'

points.label: School actions
points.text: Write, read, draw, color, count, learn, teach, play

example.problem: What action word means to make pictures with pencil?

slides.inSimpleWords: Write, read, draw, and play are daily actions.

slides.title: Feeling and Thinking
slides.storyContext: At the zoo, Arjun sees the lion. 'I'm scared!' Mitthu sees shiny mangoes. 'I like mangoes!' Arjun thinks about what to buy. 'I think!' Mitthu smiles. 'Like, love, fear, think, know, understand, wish — these are feeling and thinking actions!'

points.label: Feeling actions
points.text: Like, love, fear, think, know, feel, understand, hope, wish

slides.inSimpleWords: Think, like, love, know are thinking actions.

slides.title: Action Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu starts a game. 'I'll do an action. You name the word!' Mitthu jumps. 'Jump!' Mitthu runs around. 'Run!' Mitthu eats a seed. 'Eat!' Arjun laughs. 'I understand! Everything we DO is an action word!'

points.label: Action word test
points.text: Can you name what the action is?

example.problem: What action word means to close your eyes and rest?

slides.inSimpleWords: Everything we do has an action word.

slides.title: Night Actions
slides.storyContext: The sun sets. Arjun yawns. 'I sleep now!' Mitthu settles on a branch. 'I rest!' Before bed, Arjun's mom hugs him. 'I love you!' Mitthu chirps. 'Sleep, rest, hug, kiss, dream — night and love actions! Every moment has an action word!'

points.label: More actions
points.text: Sleep, rest, dream, hug, kiss, love, help, care

slides.inSimpleWords: Sleep, hug, and love are actions we do.

slides.title: All Kinds of Actions
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on the headboard as Arjun drifts to sleep. 'Action words tell us what we DO. Move, eat, talk, read, play, think, feel, sleep — all actions! Everything we do has an action word!'

points.label: Action words (verbs)
points.text: Tell us what we do, feel, think, or say

points.label: All kinds
points.text: Moving, eating, talking, reading, playing, thinking, feeling, sleeping

slides.inSimpleWords: Action words tell us what we do, say, or feel.

image.alt: All Kinds of Actions — Action Words
